description: Fixture versions this repo measures against, content-addressed by sha256, with the baselines recorded on each. A bar belongs to a (model, fixture, binary) triple; it is never a constant in a script. Each fixture also records the taxonomy version its labels were adjudicated under — the content digest of labels/definitions_*.yaml at the commit named in taxonomy.commit — so a score stays attributable to a vocabulary even after the taxonomy moves.

gold-2026-07-14.note: Gold corpus as of the technology.filesystem.filename adjudication; 106 columns added and 37 labels re-adjudicated since gold-2026-06-28.

m2v8m-s43/composed-reframe/0.6.53.note: 931 of the fixture's 1037 rows are scored: the 2026-06-22 corpus-pass FTMB does not cover the 106 columns added since.

m2v8m-s43/native-profile-header-raw/0.6..pipeline: finetype profile over the gold rows' own source files (multi-column, full value depth) -> x-finetype-label vs curated_label
m2v8m-s43/native-profile-header-raw/0.6..note: NOT the gold headline and NOT comparable to it: a different pipeline (native profile with the validation veto, not predict_multibranch -> compose) and a different subset (828 of the fixture's 1037 rows — 762 source files that are present locally with a unique file stem). Recorded because it is the ONLY ground-truthed instrument that can see sibling context at all: the headline's FTMB is one singleton group per column, and singletons are never enriched. Header branch served RAW header embeddings.

m2v8m-s43/native-profile-header-sibling-.pipeline: finetype profile over the gold rows' own source files (multi-column, full value depth) -> x-finetype-label vs curated_label
m2v8m-s43/native-profile-header-sibling-.note: Same 828 rows, same files, header branch served SIBLING-ENRICHED embeddings. The two directions disagree on 7 of 828 columns (4 the enriched direction gets right, 3 the raw one does); a 1-column margin on 828 rows is not a result.

corpus-oracle-2026-06-07.note: Corpus-scale A/B instrument, not an accuracy fixture. The gated-YDF oracle over the corpus-honest gate's stratified GitTables sample (output/corpus-honest-gate/stratified_sample.files.txt sha256 f99196a8da4f5a18ec4617dc27b39aecc347cfaa6ed8039868760c0010a83741, 33,250 paths, 33,054 reconstructible from eval/gittables/corpus_pass/columns.parquet sha256 de1d05b18835352d89297151aab0d00123cdc704d2d9f4ebde7cabe3a8822c97 = 837,625 columns). rows = the oracle parquet's own 1,811,352 rows (the whole corpus pass); 693,499 of the 837,625 sample columns are adjudicable, because the oracle NULLs any YDF label fewer than half the column's values pass. The oracle is a column-intrinsic MODEL, so an absolute agreement rate here is NOT an accuracy claim — only the difference between two pipelines scored against the same oracle carries meaning. The sample is ~3% of GitTables, non-adversarial, stratified on a retired model's calls, and 10.3% of its columns sit in tables whose headers are pandas artefacts.

m2v8m-s43/oracle-agreement-header-raw/0..pipeline: profile --raw-model over the reconstructed sample tables -> resharpen -> agreement with ydf_prediction_gated
m2v8m-s43/oracle-agreement-header-raw/0..note: Header branch served RAW header embeddings — what the repo ships.

m2v8m-s43/oracle-agreement-header-siblin.pipeline: profile --raw-model over the reconstructed sample tables -> resharpen -> agreement with ydf_prediction_gated
m2v8m-s43/oracle-agreement-header-siblin.note: Header branch served SIBLING-ENRICHED embeddings — training conditions reproduced. Same reconstructed tables (all 33,054 CSVs byte-identical across the two runs) and the same Sharpen stage (composed output byte-identical when both binaries resharpen one Sense cache), so the difference is attributable to the header input alone.
